reply_text:
Please don't merge this yet. The dedupe doesn't work for the case it's meant to handle: when two lists overlap, the shared contacts still come out twice. The tests pass, but they don't cover that case.

**Blocker: `src/dedupe.js` removes repeats by object, not by id**
`[...new Set(contacts)]` only drops an entry if it's the exact same object in memory. Your README says overlapping imports give you the same id on a different object, and that "Identity is the id, never object identity." So two separate imports that both contain contact `id: 1` produce two copies. I ran it to check:

```
mergeImports([{id:1,name:'Ada'}], [{id:1,name:'Ada'}])
→ [ { id: 1, name: 'Ada' }, { id: 1, name: 'Ada' } ]
```

A fix that keeps the first contact seen for each id, as the README promises:
```js
function dedupe(contacts) {
  const seen = new Set();
  return contacts.filter((c) => !seen.has(c.id) && seen.add(c.id));
}
```

**Tests don't catch it**
- `test/dedupe.test.js` only tests the same object passed in twice, which is the one case `Set` already handles. Add a test with two different objects that share an id, and check that the first one is kept.
- `mergeImports` has no tests. One test merging two overlapping lists would have caught this bug.

**Minor**
- `byName` in `src/order.js` is fine. It copies the list before sorting, so the input isn't changed, and contacts with no name are handled.
- The version bump to 2.2.0, the CHANGELOG entry and the README sections all look right, once the code matches what the README describes.

I didn't make any changes.
